clue.text: Bond part's embracing belle periodically? Cool!

indicators.note: the portions word holds the alternate letters of belle, wrapping around them

parts.note: read as 'parts', i.e. portions or shares, which are rations

indicators.note: periodically means taking every other letter of belle, at regular intervals

parts.note: hip is slang for cool or fashionable

explanation.surface: A film fan asks whether a Bond role involves clinching a beauty, and finds that cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' looks like 007 but is the definition; 'part's' is read as the plural 'parts'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond between people is a connection or tie, the same as a link of kinship or affection.

clue.text: Renew section of forest or ecosystem

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A conservation plan to bring back part of a woodland or habitat.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew something is to bring it back to its former good condition, a straight synonym.

clue.text: American measures to imprison old lags

indicators.note: to imprison means the measures word locks the letter for old inside it

parts.note: liters is the American spelling of the metric unit of volume

explanation.surface: A US prison system uses measures to lock up seasoned convicts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lags' looks like a noun (old lags are habitual convicts) but is the verb: dawdles.
explanation.definitionFit: To lag is to fall behind or dawdle, much as someone hanging about idly does.

clue.text: Revolving apparatus for fans?

parts.note: fans here are spectators at a ground: the rotating gate they push through one at a time to enter, not a cooling fan's rotor

explanation.surface: Sounds like a description of a ceiling fan's spinning mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports supporters enter stadiums through rotating barred gates that admit one person at a time.

clue.text: Leered over girl looking extremely dodgy initially

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of each of the five words before it is taken

explanation.surface: A creep looks over a girl in an extremely shifty way.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer is to look at someone with unpleasant desire, as a lecherous starer does.

clue.text: Marine worker enclosing large water barrier?

indicators.note: enclosing means the marine and worker pieces surround the letter for large

parts.note: marine means of the sea
ant is the crossword's stock worker insect
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A sailor or diver builds a big barrier against the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition: a waterproofing compound keeps water out.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproofing compound is applied to joints to stop moisture getting through, a barrier against leaks.

clue.text: Head of pin piercing bug for study

indicators.note: piercing means the letter from pin goes through, so sits inside, the bug word

parts.note: a bug is an insect

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of pin

explanation.surface: An entomologist pins a specimen through the body to examine it.
explanation.definitionFit: To study something closely is to examine or scrutinise it carefully.

clue.text: A sect's cilice prepared for cleric

indicators.note: prepared means the letters are made ready in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A religious group gets a hair shirt ready for a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: A cilice is a penitential hair shirt, which suits the religious picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the clergy, a churchman, is a cleric.

clue.text: Bank clerk is cold and comparatively grey

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ashy means grey like ash, so more grey is ashier

explanation.surface: A description of a pale, chilly bank employee.
explanation.definitionFit: The person at a bank counter who pays out and takes in money is a teller.

clue.text: Established contact fibbed about top story's lead

indicators.note: about means the fibbing word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: fibbed means told a lie
A1 means top quality; the figure 1 is written as the letter I

indicators.note: lead means the first letter of story's

explanation.surface: Someone lied to make contact with the source of a top news story.
explanation.walkthrough: AI stands for A1, first-rate, with the digit read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to work in cooperation and communicate with another party.

clue.text: Navigated badly, circling wretched albatross?

indicators.note: circling means the jumbled letters surround the wretched word
badly means the letters of navigated are jumbled up

parts.note: wretched means sad, miserable

explanation.surface: A sailor steered poorly while circling a seabird in distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'albatross' looks like the bird the sailor circles; it is a burden, as in Coleridge's Ancient Mariner.
explanation.definitionFit: An albatross around one's neck is a burden or handicap, from Coleridge's poem, so a figurative drawback.

clue.text: Frees from lavatory feeling unfinished

parts.note: loo is British slang for a lavatory

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a sense is a feeling

explanation.surface: Someone escapes from a toilet with a sense of something left undone.
explanation.definitionFit: To free something is to slacken or undo it, making it less tight.

clue.text: Small compensation returning lingerie?

indicators.note: returning means the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: a reward is compensation or recompense

explanation.surface: A shopper gets a small refund on returned underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: knickers are lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-fashioned knickers or underpants are a kind of women's underwear.

clue.text: Wise people, ushers occasionally, protecting Queen

indicators.note: protecting means the alternate letters wrap around the Queen
occasionally means every other letter of ushers is used

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Sages and ushers sometimes act as royal bodyguards.
explanation.definitionFit: Prophets and visionaries are wise figures who can foresee events.

clue.text: Angry discontented influencer judged about sex

indicators.note: discontented means the contents are removed, leaving the outer letters of influencer
about means the judged word goes around the sex word

parts.note: rated means judged or assessed
it is slang for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: An unhappy social-media influencer is cross after being judged over sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' means emptied of its contents, not unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being annoyed or vexed means being angry.

clue.text: Logic of AI to learn differently

indicators.note: differently means the letters are arranged in a different order

explanation.surface: Artificial intelligence must learn reasoning in a new way.
explanation.definitionFit: The reasoning or justification behind something is its underlying logic.

clue.text: Receptive sailor shipped around globe

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor

indicators.note: around means the shipped word goes around the globe word

parts.note: sent means shipped or dispatched
an orb is a globe or sphere

explanation.surface: An open-minded sailor is sent off around the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that soaks up liquid readily is receptive in the physical sense.

clue.text: Exercising brains to catch European national

indicators.note: to catch means the rearranged letters hold the European abbreviation
exercising means the letters of brains are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Using one's wits to apprehend a citizen of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of a Balkan country is one of its nationals.

clue.text: Rugby supporter keeps providing backing for lout

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union

indicators.note: keeps means the supporter word holds the reversed piece

parts.note: a fan is a supporter

indicators.note: backing means the providing word is read backwards

parts.note: if means providing, as in 'providing that'

explanation.surface: A rugby fan keeps backing his team, yet behaves like a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support for a team; it signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A lout is a rough, violent hooligan or thug.

clue.text: Good person, with look back, streaks

definitions.note: the clue gives a plural, though the entry is the singular; its plural adds E

parts.note: ST, for saint, is the crossword's good person

indicators.note: back means the look word is read backwards

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: A virtuous person glances back at stripes.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a single linear mark, but the clue's 'streaks' is plural, a looseness by the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stria is a thin groove or linear mark, as in stretch marks or rock grooves.

clue.text: Dexterity of sweetheart in dainty embrace

indicators.note: embrace means the dainty word wraps around the sweetheart letter

parts.note: slight means small and delicate, dainty
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: A lover shows nimbleness in a gentle hug.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is manual skill, so the word alone means dexterity or deftness.

clue.text: About lost power keeping America prepared

indicators.note: keeping means the outer pieces hold the America letter

parts.note: re means about, concerning
an engine that has lost power has died

explanation.surface: Something about a US power cut and getting ready for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something ready is to prepare it.

clue.text: Rates a Republican wearing spats

indicators.note: wearing means the spats word has the other pieces inside it, as clothing holds a wearer

parts.note: spats are petty quarrels, tiffs

explanation.surface: A dapper Republican in old-fashioned ankle-gaiters, with talk of tax rates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spats' looks like the gaiters a well-dressed figure might wear; it is quarrels.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs duties and charges are rates levied on imports.

clue.text: Follow on, say, in charge

indicators.note: in means the example abbreviation sits inside the charge word

parts.note: to sue is to bring a legal charge
say means for example, EG

explanation.surface: Someone takes over, in charge, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth transition from one thing into the next means to follow on without a break.

clue.text: Part of lover, actually ham!

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An actor playing a romantic role is overdoing it, as in Love Actually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' is a verb here, to perform with exaggeration.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham it up is to perform in a showy, exaggerated way.

clue.text: Reportedly spot fish in vault?

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are said aloud and an identically sounding word is entered

parts.note: to spot is to see; ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Word has it a fish was spotted in a bank vault.
explanation.walkthrough: A vault is an arched roof; the question mark marks it as an example of the overhead surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaulted roof is an arched overhead surface inside a building, the top of a room.

clue.text: Seeking perch, perhaps flapping, losing head

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: dangling means hanging loosely, flapping

explanation.surface: A bird flaps about looking for somewhere to land, then loses its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' looks like a bird's roost; it is the freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishing with rod and line, after perch for example, is the sport of the rod.

clue.text: Bored denture set in, somehow

indicators.note: somehow means the letters are put together in some new order

explanation.surface: A patient is fed up having false teeth fitted somehow.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bored shows no curiosity or concern, feeling indifferent and listless.
